summary: SSE sentence truncation after edge connection-pool reuse
description: Issue summary: Several customers (first reported by Keynote Analytics) observe that SSE-based streaming responses occasionally drop the final sentence of the assistant output after an upstream edge connection is reused from the CDN/edge pool. Impact: Partial outputs cause downstream NLP pipelines to mis-parse JSON-like structured completions and break end-user UX in conversation flows. Scope: Reported sporadically across long-running multi-paragraph responses; appears correlated with high connection-pool reuse and certain edge proxy keep-alive settings. Environment: Production (us-east), customers on enterprise plan using hosted Redwood API via our public endpoint; affected models include openchat-3b and redwood-compat-7b. Steps to reproduce (approx): 1) Launch a streaming SSE request with an intentionally long response (5+ paragraphs) using curl: curl -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=openchat-3b" 2) Simulate high edge reuse by firing many short requests from the same client IP to warm the CDN pool, then issue the long streaming request. 3) Observe final events and check for truncated last sentence or missing terminal "event: done" semantics. Observed behavior: The stream completes at the server (trace shows final tokens emitted) but the client receives a truncated last sentence in the final SSE chunk and sometimes does not receive the terminal end-event. The phenomenon spikes when the edge proxy responds with a 200 and then the connection is reused immediately for the SSE session (half-closed socket reuse). Expected behavior: Complete final sentence and terminal SSE event delivered consistently. Logs / traces: - api-gw request id: rgw-2a4f9c - backend serving logs show complete token stream: "... final sentence concluding the assistant's thought.\n" - edge proxy (nginx-lb) logs show connection reset or keep-alive rebind around same timestamp, followed by immediate downstream connection acceptance. Suspected root cause: Edge connection-pool reuse triggers a half-closed socket state where the final chunk (small trailing bytes) is coalesced or dropped by certain proxy rewrite/flush timing. This is exacerbated when Transfer-Encoding: chunked interactions and SSE heartbeat coalesce. Attachments: request/response curl transcripts, sanitized logs, packet capture (pcap) from customer (on-file), Slack thread link.
investigation_notes: 03/10 16:20 - Support: Verified customer replay and captured server-side token emission. 03/10 18:05 - SRE: Reproduced locally using an nginx front with keepalive_timeout=1s and many short warm requests; saw identical truncation pattern. 03/11 09:12 - Engineering hypothesized edge flush race: final chunk arrives at proxy but proxy performs connection handback/pool reuse before flush to client socket. 03/11 12:00 - Added additional debug to serving-runtime to log final write/flush syscall timing; server shows final write succeeded, kernel ACKs present, but client-side event stream missing last bytes. 03/11 15:30 - Confirmed reproducible when nginx proxy has sendfile on and tcp_nodelay off; disabling sendfile or increasing keepalive_timeout mitigates reproduction. 03/12 10:00 - Performed controlled test across eu-west and us-east; only edge proxies with connection pooling timeout <2s exhibited issue.
steps_taken: 1) Eng escalated to infra and edge teams; created short-lived lab with nginx/varnish variants. 2) Reproduced with nginx config: keepalive_timeout=1; sendfile on; tcp_nodelay off. 3) Verified mitigation: setting sendfile off OR tcp_nodelay on reduces occurrence. 4) Implemented temporary workaround in routing policy to avoid reusing edge connection for streaming requests by adding 'Connection: close' upstream hint for flagged customers. 5) Notified Keynote Analytics of temporary mitigation and asked for consent to enable customer-level flag.
current_workaround: Support enabled per-customer upstream hint to set 'Connection: close' for SSE streaming sessions for Keynote Analytics; this prevents pool reuse and restores complete final-sentence delivery at the cost of additional TCP handshakes. Customer confirmed improved results for their failing flows.
